text: Paradoxically, the standard model of rational choice, by assuming that people always make the single best decision, actually strips away our agency and limits freedom of choice. <break time="0.8s" /> In this way of thinking, the perfectly rational Homo economicus does not really have any options, they are expected to always pick just the very best one. <break time="0.8s" /> If they do anything different, their actions are either ignored or simply called irrational, the rational economic actor is paradoxically constrained by the models limited definition of what counts as good behavior. <break time="0.8s" /> By insisting on a single, rigid standard of rationality, the mainstream model ironically denies the very thing it claims to uphold, the human capacity for reason and self determination. <break time="0.8s" /> In this sense, the rational choice model is not just descriptively inaccurate but also prescriptively dangerous. <break time="0.8s" /> By holding up Homo economicus as the standard to which all behavior should converge, it creates a kind of economic peer pressure that stigmatizes and punishes anyone who does not fit the mold. <break time="0.8s" /> It says, in effect, You are not rational enough, so you are not good enough.
